Answer: D
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates situs inversus totalis, characterized by dextrocardia (heart apex pointing to the right) and a gastric air bubble located beneath the right hemidiaphragm (mirror image of normal). In this mirrored anatomy, the horizontal fissure is found in the left hemithorax (associated with the morphological right lung on the left side), which supports the diagnosis of Kartagener syndrome when combined with clinical history. Option B is incorrect because it describes the stomach bubble on the left (normal situs), and Option A describes levocardia.
